warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor on purpose. The architect, the four workers, the five auditors and this red team are all one model family (claude-opus-5), and an isolated context is not an independent vendor. What actually holds here is the deterministic layer: the machine gates, the frozen check_plan

Write access to raw sources and frozen machinery was blocked by permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json only for edit tools, not for the shell. A modified raw file would have been caught afterwards by the control lock, not prevented.

The LLM auditor layer of this run is empty in substance. gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor and gate_release_auditor all have 'driver e2e' summaries and evidence notes with one placeholder line, and their 'recomputed independently' checks repeat the machine

All four worker results are placeholders. Each reports a self-check 'recomputed independently' with expected and actual 0.473684, a number that appears nowhere in this audit, and a created_at of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, before this run. None carries a disclosures field. That no worker disclosed a devia

The two test cards in release/dashboard_data.json show value 0.0000 under the labels 'Test Channel Completion' and 'Test Channel Aov', with no sign that the value is a p-value and no alpha or hypothesis. A dashboard reader can take 0.0000 as a completion or AOV figure.
Both p-values are shown as 0.0000 in report.md and the dashboard, not as below 0.0001. The p is not zero: z = 26.72 and Welch t = 42.70 at about 28,537 degrees of freedom.

The caveat 'one quarter of orders in this channel' and the report sentence 'an estimate from one quarter of orders' can be read as a 25 percent sample, not as one calendar quarter. The figures are the whole quarter's export, and the interval treats that quarter as a sample of an ongoing process.

The AOV lines and cards never state that AOV is over delivered orders only and net of refunds, and the dashboard has no population field on any card. The release contract declares no card_caveat_requirements and no reconciliations, so nothing deterministic checks card-level populations.

Human decision dedup_rule (latest_revision_wins): 549 of the 917 repeated orders have identical updated_at on both revisions, and 6 of the 126 status changes between revisions fall in those ties, so for those orders 'latest' rests on file order alone. The rule moves net revenue from 3,010,704.83 (fi

Human decision refund_sign_policy excludes whole orders, not just the faulty refund field. 10 in-quarter orders are excluded (8 delivered, 9 of them direct), which moves CLM-ORDERS by 10 and the direct completion denominator by 9. Keeping them with a zero refund would add 967.93 EUR to net revenue.

Human decisions date_input_formats (month-first slashes) and the Europe/Warsaw timezone move no published number. No slashed date has a first field above 12 and 4,197 have a second field above 12. Every clean order_date month equals order_month, the period is taken on order_month, and no ISO-8601 Z

Human decision shipping_locale is consistent with the data: no cell mixes a dot and a comma, and my own parser reproduces shipping_total 37,792,722.50, versus 1,248,402,183.11 if separators were stripped. But the column's scale looks implausible for these orders: an average of about 849 EUR shipping
Net revenue is the booked value of delivered orders net of refunds, not cash received. The 7,491 pending orders are outside it by definition, and nothing on the page speaks to payment timing.

The check plan puts no deterministic rule on carry content, on what a caveat means (caveats_declared and caveats_rendered match substrings only), on the report's page-level population line, or on dashboard labels and n. Those are exactly where this run's defects sit, and more is unchecked there than

The handoff carries no drift_since_review, which does not prove that the stage code's assumptions hold on this export. No audit/decisions/*.json exists and rulings is empty, so no number here rests on a logged ruling and no method was changed after results existed.

summary: Every published number reproduces exactly from the quarantine projection with my own code (49 of 49 comparisons, clean table equal to the declared population row by row, 60 of 60 surface numbers bound, nothing unbound). The release still fails on meaning. First, the partner completion caveat says the reverse of the spec: it claims the interval also covers a changing country mix, and the same page says the interval is the sampling interval and nothing else.
